It runs eager by default, compiles through torch.compile and XLA, and replaces PyTorch/XLA for new workloads. The post Google Open-Sources TorchTPU, a Native PyTorch Backend for Cloud TPUs appeared first on MarkTechPost . ]]> Google has open-sourced TorchTPU , a native PyTorch backend for Cloud TPUs. It was co-developed with the PyTorch team at Meta and announced at PyTorch Conference 2026 on October 20, 2026. Existing PyTorch code targets a TPU through a standard torch.device("tpu") . TPUs now sit beside GPUs and CPUs as a native PyTorch device. Google team states that TorchTPU replaces PyTorch/XLA and recommends it for all new workloads. TL;DR Size: A software stack, not a model. 4 open repos: TorchTPU, vLLM-TorchTPU, SGLang-TorchTPU, TorchTitan. TorchTPU is v0.2.0 on PyPI , Python 3.11+, Apache 2.0. Runs on: Google Cloud TPUs. Tested on generations from v5e , scaled to 8,192 Ironwood (TPU7x) chips. Serving supports FP8, MXFP4 and NVFP4 checkpoints. Performance: Eager mode for debugging, torch.compile for production-level throughput. Best: 52% MFU training Qwen 3 8B with TorchTitan on Ironwood (self-reported). Worst: Out-of-box eager took 11.49s per step in a fine-tuning case, versus 2.78s fully tuned. What is TorchTPU? TorchTPU is an open-source PyTorch backend from Google and Meta that runs PyTorch models natively on TPUs. It plugs in through PyTorch’s PrivateUse1 interface . Tensors are ordinary PyTorch tensors, with no subclasses or wrappers. It runs one process per device and preserves tensor views and in-place mutations. The predecessor, PyTorch/XLA, recorded lazy-tensor graphs. Developers often added code to mark compilable regions. PyTorch/XLA also only supported pure SPMD code . TorchTPU also handles divergent MPMD execution. How does TorchTPU execute PyTorch code? TorchTPU ships 3 eager modes : Strict (default): dispatches each operator asynchronously with standard PyTorch semantics. Debug: runs synchronously with tensor bounds checking. DeferAndFuse: fuses runs of eager operators to cut HBM traffic. The TorchTPU paper says it can be 50% or more faster than Strict. For peak speed, torch.compile(backend="tpu") captures the graph with TorchDynamo. It lowers through StableHLO to OpenXLA, which emits TPU machine code. Compiled executables are cached across processes, hosts and job restarts. Custom Pallas kernels are callable as standard PyTorch functions. Prebuilt Tokamax kernels and Helion tile kernels also work. Distribution uses the tpu_dist process group. It supports DDP, FSDP2 and DTensor, along with a topology-aware mesh for TPU interconnects. How fast is TorchTPU? All figures below are self-reported by Google and partners. Training scale: TorchTitan reached up to 52% MFU on Qwen 3 8B . Google reports near-linear scaling up to 8,192 Ironwood TPUs. Tuning ladder: In a TorchTitan fine-tuning case, step time fell from 11.49s to 2.78s. DeferAndFuse alone gave 1.15x. Full torch.compile gave 3.80x . Model coverage: Google continuously tests about 5,000 Hugging Face models in eager and compiled modes. Fleet serving: Zenteiq grew daily output from 1.47B to 5.97B tokens per 1,000 TPU v6e chips. That gain came from llm-d routing on GKE, not TorchTPU alone. What integrations ship with TorchTPU? Hugging Face: Transformers v5 deploys to TPU with device_map="tpu" . Diffusers supports eager, torch.compile and tensor parallelism. vLLM-TorchTPU : built with Inferact. Keeps upstream schedulers and API servers, with custom Pallas kernels. SGLang-TorchTPU : built with RadixArk. Keeps RadixAttention prefix reuse. Serving features: FP8 KV caches, FP8, MXFP4 and NVFP4 checkpoints. Speculative decoding includes MTP and EAGLE-3. TorchTitan : recipes for Llama 3 70B/405B, Qwen 3 8B/32B, Qwen 3 235B MoE and FLUX.1 12B. Also: llm-d 1.0, Ray, TorchRec, VeRL (preview) and LiteRT-Torch for on-device export. How does TorchTPU compare with PyTorch/XLA, TorchNeuron and JAX? Feature TorchTPU ( repo ) PyTorch/XLA ( repo ) TorchNeuron ( AWS docs ) JAX on TPU ( Google docs ) Vendor Google + Meta Google / PyTorch AWS Google Hardware Cloud TPU (v5e and later tested) Cloud TPU Trainium 2, Trainium 3 Cloud TPU PyTorch device tpu xla neuron Not PyTorch Backend mechanism PrivateUse1 Lazy-tensor graph recording PrivateUse1 Not applicable Default execution Eager (Strict, Debug, DeferAndFuse) Lazy tensors Eager plus torch.compile Not disclosed Compile path TorchDynamo to StableHLO to XLA XLA Neuron Compiler XLA Distributed APIs DDP, FSDP2, DTensor, SPMD and MPMD Pure SPMD only FSDP, DTensor, DDP, TP Not disclosed Custom kernels Pallas, Tokamax, Helion Not disclosed NKI Pallas vLLM / SGLang serving vLLM-TorchTPU, SGLang-TorchTPU Not disclosed vLLM Neuron vLLM-JAX, SGLang-JAX Status Open source, v0.2.0 Being replaced by TorchTPU Public beta (Neuron 2.33) Maintained License Apache 2.0 Not disclosed Not disclosed Not disclosed How do you install TorchTPU? Install the package on a TPU VM, then pick the tpu device: Copy Code Copied Use a different Browser # pip install torch_tpu import torch device = torch.device("tpu") x = torch.randn((4, 4), device=device) The repo’s README pins torch_tpu==0.2.0 with the CPU PyTorch wheel index. Without it, pip pulls the CUDA build of torch . Full guides live at torchtpu.readthedocs.io . Key Takeaways TorchTPU is open source under Apache 2.0, co-built with Meta. It replaces PyTorch/XLA with eager-first, PrivateUse1-based execution. torch.compile(backend="tpu") lowers through StableHLO and XLA. TorchTitan hit 52% MFU on Qwen 3 8B, scaling to 8,192 Ironwood chips. vLLM, SGLang and Hugging Face now run on TPU through standard PyTorch. Mistral Voxtral 3 is a speech model family paired with a voice agent SDK. It ships 3 transcription models, 1 text-to-speech model and an SDK built on LiveKit. One place for listening, reasoning, tool calls and speaking. All 4 models are in public preview on the Mistral API. TL;DR Size: Voxtral Mini Transcribe 3 has 4B parameters. Small Transcribe 3 size: not disclosed. Both batch models list a 32k context . Runs on: Mistral API (EU, US and global endpoints) or your own infrastructure via Mistral sales. GPU and VRAM needs: not disclosed. Mistral says Mini suits resource-constrained environments . Performance: Top 3 on independent speech-to-text rankings, strongest on diarization and multilingual batch transcription. Best: 2.1% AA-WER for Small Transcribe 3, #3 on Artificial Analysis . Worst: Realtime at 240 ms: 7.4% WER on FLEURS 35, vs 4.2% for Gemini 3.5 Realtime. What is in the Voxtral 3 family? Mistral lists 4 models and 1 SDK: Voxtral Small Transcribe 3 : flagship batch transcription and diarization. Docs also list translation, speech Q&A, summarization and function calling. Voxtral Mini Transcribe 3 : a 4B model for cheaper, faster batch jobs. Voxtral Mini Transcribe Realtime 3 : streaming ASR over WebSocket with end-of-turn detection. Voxtral Speech 3 : text-to-speech, also called Voxtral Mini TTS 3 in the post. All transcription models support diarization and context biasing. Context biasing takes key terms or free text to improve recall. Batch transcription covers 50 languages, including 24 official EU languages. How does the Voxtral voice agent SDK work? The SDK is built on LiveKit and runs 3 stages as 1 streaming pipeline. Realtime Transcribe 3 listens and detects when the caller stops speaking. A general LLM, such as Mistral Small 4 , reasons and calls tools. Voxtral Speech 3 replies in the tone of the conversation so far. Each turn completes in under 1 second. The agent stops talking when the caller cuts in. It handles phone calls over SIP and browser or app sessions over WebRTC. Because each stage is a separate model, teams can swap the LLM, voice or language. How accurate is Voxtral Transcribe 3? These numbers are self-reported by Mistral: FLEURS 45 (WER, forced / inferred language): Small 4.1% / 4.0%. MAI-Transcribe-2 ties at 4.1% / 4.0%. Mini 4.6% / 4.5%. Whisper large-v3 16.0% / 14.9%. Diarization (cpWER, 5 public sets): Small 18.4% and Mini 18.6%. Pyannote scores 19.0% and MAI-Transcribe-2 20.3%. Keyphrase recall (Earnings 22): Small 94.6% with context, 81.4% without. Scribe v2 posts 94.3% and 84.0%. On Artificial Analysis , Small scores 2.1% AA-WER and Mini 2.2%. Only Fun-Realtime-ASR-preview (1.7%) and MAI-Transcribe-2 (2.0%) rank higher. Speed is the gap: Small’s speed factor is 65.8x, against 307.5x for MAI-Transcribe-2. How do realtime transcription and TTS compare? On FLEURS 35, the realtime model trades latency for accuracy. It scores 5.7% WER at 2,400 ms and 6.4% at 480 ms. At 240 ms, WER rises to 7.4%. Gemini 3.5 Realtime Transcribe scores 4.2% and MAI-Transcribe-2 Streaming 5.8%. GPT Live Transcribe (8.4%) and Scribe v2 Realtime (8.7%) trail every Voxtral setting. Voxtral Speech 3 costs $13 per 1M characters. Mistral says that undercuts OpenAI TTS-1, Deepgram, ElevenLabs Flash and Gemini Flash. Explicit controls cover emotion , pacing and emphasis . The model page lists ~90 ms time-to-first-audio and 34 emotion tags. Pro Voice adapts a speaker’s style from 30 minutes of audio. Artificial Analysis places it in the top 12 of both TTS arenas . oldContent: Crunchbase News https://news.crunchbase.com/ Data-driven reporting on private markets, startups, founders, and investors Mon, 19 Oct 2026 17:23:06 +0000 en-US hourly 1 https://wordpress.org/?v=6.8.11 https://news.crunchbase.com/wp-content/uploads/cb_news_favicon-150x150.png Crunchbase News https://news.crunchbase.com/ 32 32 How To Build A Billion-Dollar Company Without Venture Capital https://news.crunchbase.com/startups/bootstrapping-billion-dollar-company-ai-staffing-demarco-bairesdev/ Tue, 20 Oct 2026 11:00:46 +0000 https://news.crunchbase.com/?p=94248 By Nacho De Marco Today’s venture capital ecosystem looks markedly different from even just five years ago. Most significantly, a small number of AI companies are now attracting the vast majority of available venture capital. In Q1 2026, just four companies collectively raised $188 billion , which alone accounted for 65% of total global venture investment, per Crunchbase data. Meanwhile, in that same quarter, just 20% of global VC funding went to non-AI firms . Deal count was also down 30%, meaning that checks are being made out to fewer companies all around. So what happens to startups when the VC route is all but closed? I built a company into a multibillion-dollar business without any venture funding. Here’s a few lessons I picked up along the way: Prioritize customers and revenue, not fundraising Nacho De Marco, founding GP of BDev Ventures, and chairman of BairesDev. Many founders unknowingly treat fundraising as a measure of success. But while it’s useful, funding doesn’t result in success on its own. Achieving strong levels of customer trust is also helpful when it comes to inspiring investor confidence. High retention rates, repeat purchases and sustained engagement drive the financial fundamentals on which strong valuations are built. In B2B SaaS, for instance, companies with net revenue retention above 110% are valued at 2.4x the median . Additionally, customers provide a feedback loop that helps create the discipline every company needs, and each user is a vote of confidence that compounds over time. Going to market: Take time on pricing strategy Too many early-stage companies set prices too low because they fear that higher prices will repel customers. In my experience, however, underpricing more often signals uncertainty rather than good value. Customers want quality products and services, and they expect that the quality will be reflected in the price. Incredibly, only 22% of B2B SaaS firms conduct rigorous pricing research , and firms more commonly regret underpricing than overpricing. So at the outset, it’s important for startups to inform themselves what price their product or service can actually sustain, and then raise quality if it’s too low. Equally, in services markets where prices are more established around a norm, superior quality can be an important differentiator. At the same time, however, companies must continually resist the temptation to chase customers with ever-cheaper prices, which can start a race to the bottom. Hire the best talent Too many founders hire for speed rather than quality. Take the time needed to raise the bar with talent. Hire the right people, and they’ll help maximize every last drop of value. Many years ago, I decided to focus on just a small fraction of our applicants and hire only the top 1% of talent . When we found the best developers, it meant we could compete on delivery quality rather than just price. Keeping costs low is important, but skimping on talent is not a winning strategy. Use process automation efficiencies to drive growth One of our best decisions was to replace manual hiring processes with proprietary machine-learning systems at an early stage. Not only do these systems screen developer applications, but they can also build, match and deploy top-quality teams for each client project. This advance allowed us to cut costs associated with evaluating applications, accelerate lead times, and improve the quality of our teamwork. In parallel, we also invested in creating similar systems for our digital marketing so that growth wouldn’t require proportional increases in overhead. Whether it’s in recruitment, sales or operations, process automation can create some of the biggest drivers of growth and help bring about conditions needed for significant expansion to occur. Operate as if cash is running out tomorrow Companies thrive in challenging funding environments by operating with discipline. That means obsessing over unit economics, prioritizing activities that directly drive revenue, questioning every cost, and eliminating anything that isn’t pulling its weight. Not only does this aid growth, but it also makes a business more resilient in hard times. Financial constraints drive leaders to create efficiencies by automating workflows, streamlining processes and inventing innovative work models. Years before COVID-19 forced others to follow our lead, our company streamlined its operations and boosted scalability by developing a remote-working model. When the pandemic made remote work necessary, the fact that we already had the systems and workflows in place gave us a competitive advantage over other firms, and this in turn led to significant growth. Long term: Stay married to the problem, not the solution The past decade convinced many founders that venture capital was the default path to building a meaningful company. But while funding cycles rise and fall, the fundamental principles of good business don’t. Infusions of capital can accelerate growth, but they cannot create a great company from scratch. On the longest timescale, the most successful founders are the ones committed to solving problems rather than just selling a product and chasing funding. In a world short on funding, growth simply can’t happen without it. Nacho De Marco is the founding GP of BDev Ventures , and chairman of BairesDev , one of the largest bootstrapped nearshoring companies worldwide. Driven by his entrepreneurial spirit, he launched BDev Ventures in 2021 to help B2B companies accelerate their growth through a proprietary lead-generation platform. He also invests in and serves on the boards of biotechnology and e-learning companies. In recognition of his career path, he won distinctions such as an EY Entrepreneur Of The Year 2024 Bay Area Award. newContent: Crunchbase News https://news.crunchbase.com/ Data-driven reporting on private markets, startups, founders, and investors Tue, 20 Oct 2026 16:10:34 +0000 en-US hourly 1 https://wordpress.org/?v=6.8.11 https://news.crunchbase.com/wp-content/uploads/cb_news_favicon-150x150.png Crunchbase News https://news.crunchbase.com/ 32 32 When A Startup Sells, Its Employees’ Equity Plans Can Change Overnight https://news.crunchbase.com/ma/acquired-startup-employees-equity-plans-from-honig/ Wed, 21 Oct 2026 11:00:38 +0000 https://news.crunchbase.com/?p=94255 By Ron Honig Acquisitions are reshaping the technology industry. Venture-backed AI companies acquired 195 AI startups this year through late September , already exceeding the total for all of 2025, Crunchbase data shows. For investors and founders, such acquisitions can represent major financial milestones. For employees holding equity compensation, a transaction can also change personal financial plans they had expected to follow for years. A client whose employer was acquired in an all-cash transaction described to me the atmosphere inside the company during the weeks that followed: Employees repeatedly discussed the deal in office corridors, trying to understand what it meant for their equity awards, their jobs and their future. She compared the confusion to the atmosphere surrounding a major reorganization or a round of layoffs. The transaction offered the prospect of substantial financial gains. Yet employees were struggling to establish what those gains would mean for them individually. One acquisition, different outcomes Ron Honig, co-CEO of From-Honig Family Office. Employees at the same company can emerge from an acquisition with remarkably different financial outcomes. Some own vested shares. Others hold restricted stock units, stock options or performance-based awards. Their rights depend on grant agreements, vesting conditions and transaction terms. Even two employees holding RSUs may face different payment schedules or employment requirements. Depending on the agreements, outstanding awards may be settled in cash, accelerated, converted into replacement awards, or remain subject to future conditions. One employee might receive a substantial payment when the transaction closes. Another may have much of the expected value tied to continued employment. The announced acquisition price provides a reference point. It rarely tells an individual employee everything they need to know about the money they will receive. This helps explain the conversations my client described. Colleagues may compare the value of their equity without realizing that their contractual rights differ. Wealth and employment uncertainty Technology employees with substantial equity compensation often depend on their employer in several ways. Their salaries, bonuses, career opportunities and investment portfolios may all be linked to the same company. An all-cash acquisition can reduce their exposure to its share price once vested shares are converted into cash. Other forms of dependence may continue. The acquiring company may reorganize teams, change responsibilities or introduce retention arrangements. Employees whose unvested awards remain conditional on employment may face difficult choices about staying. Someone expecting a large payment can therefore feel financially stronger while becoming less certain about their career. Before making plans A major acquisition announcement can change personal ambitions long before the proceeds arrive. Employees may begin considering early retirement, a new business, a career break or a major family purchase. Those possibilities are worth exploring. But an announced acquisition may still require regulatory approvals and other closing conditions. The headline value of an equity award may differ substantially from the cash ultimately available to its holder. Taxes, exercise costs where applicable, outstanding liabilities and payment schedules can all affect the outcome. So can the employee’s financial position outside the company. A substantial payment might make a career change affordable without providing enough capital to fund permanent retirement. Existing pension savings, household spending and future earning capacity remain important. In my work with technology executives, I have seen expectations about new wealth reshape personal plans before the underlying numbers have been established. Employees facing a cash acquisition can begin with three questions: What rights do my specific awards provide? When will the proceeds actually become available? And what choices will the resulting after-tax capital support? The answers may differ considerably among colleagues. An exit without an exit decision Founders who sell their companies often participate directly in negotiating the transaction. Employees holding equity compensation generally have much less influence over its timing. They may have intended to retain their shares for years, sell gradually or remain employed until additional awards vested. A corporate acquisition can replace those plans with a timetable established by the transaction. For some employees, the result will be substantial financial flexibility. For others, a significant part of their expected compensation may remain connected to future employment. The period between announcement and closing can be especially difficult because the financial opportunity is visible while important details remain unresolved. My client’s description of the office corridors captured that experience. The company had made a decision about its future. Its employees were left to work out what that decision meant for theirs. The acquisition determines the terms of a corporate transaction. Each employee still has to establish how much financial freedom it creates. "Up" means uptime, reliability, and acceleration. "Sun" reflects our follow-the-sun-support, a 24x7, globally distributed support team keeping the lights on while you rest. Our core belief is that software should power brighter solutions and greater innovation. </span></p> <p><span>Upsunners are a remote, global workforce, and we thrive in a multicultural team. We are committed to open source and an open, welcoming environment. Our team spans the globe and the experience spectrum. </span></p> <p><span>What's our commonality, our cultural fabric? A curious spirit and a thirst for knowledge; an eagerness for innovative ideas and cultures. We believe we can build anything together in an environment that frees you to do your best work. </span></p> <p><span>Our values:&nbsp;</span></p> <p><span> We make a positive impact.</span></p> <p><span> We aim for the stars.</span></p> <p><span> We care for each other.&nbsp;</span></p> <h1><span><strong>Impact of a Product Manager</strong></span></h1> <p><span>As a Product Manager at Upsun, you own a significant area of Upsun Cloud, our cloud application platform, and the outcomes it delivers for the developers who build on it. The team you join owns the platform's foundations: the API, the runtime, environments, and the reliability every application running on Upsun depends on. And because Upsun is the cloud application platform humans and robots love, much of what you build will be used by AI agents as much as by people.</span></p> <p><span>This is a hands-on, technically rich role that bridges product strategy and deep infrastructure understanding. You own the strategy and the roadmap for your area, working closely with engineering to define platform behavior, build scalable abstractions, and shape workflows that empower modern development teams. Throughout, you act as the key voice for the user, making sure everything we ship contributes meaningfully to an exceptional developer experience.</span></p> <h1><span><strong>What to Founded in 2008 and profitable since 2014, our annual revenue is in the hundreds of millions USD and millions use our browser on <a class="ProsemirrorEditor-link" href="https://spreadprivacy.com/introducing-duckduckgo-for-mac/">Mac</a>, <a class="ProsemirrorEditor-link" href="https://spreadprivacy.com/windows-browser-open-beta/">Windows</a>, <a class="ProsemirrorEditor-link" href="https://spreadprivacy.com/duckduckgo-privacy-browser-ios14/">iOS</a>, and <a class="ProsemirrorEditor-link" href="https://spreadprivacy.com/introducing-app-tracking-protection/">Android</a>, our <a class="ProsemirrorEditor-link" href="https://duckduckgo.com/">search engine</a>, and the <a class="ProsemirrorEditor-link" href="https://duckduckgo.com/pro">DuckDuckGo subscription</a>. We also offer private, useful, and optional AI, including <a class="ProsemirrorEditor-link" href="https://duck.ai/">Duck.ai</a>, which lets you chat privately with ChatGPT, Claude, and other AIs, all in one place.</p> <div>&nbsp;</div> <p>Our <a class="ProsemirrorEditor-link" href="https://duckduckgo.com/how-we-work">culture</a> of trust, inclusivity, and empowered project management underpins everything we do, where each team member takes full ownership of their projects, from scoping and execution to postmortem. If you're seeking end-to-end ownership of your work, you've come to the right place!</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <h1><strong>Your Team and Role</strong></h1> <p>Working on the Backend Functional Team, you'll lead complex projects across key company-wide objectives. Using Perl (Version 5), Go, and Node.js, you’ll write pragmatic, performant, testable code that works consistently, and work on related projects. Recent projects include:</p> <ul> <li> <p>Implementing AI-assisted answers and integrating them into our Search product while maintaining our privacy-first approach</p> </li> <li> <p>Delivering improvements to Duck.ai to help us make it a competitive AI chat alternative for both free and paying users</p> </li> <li> <p>Implementing sophisticated data processing pipelines that maintain search relevancy</p> </li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p>As a <strong>Senior Backend Engineer</strong>, you'll collaborate remotely with your peers and take responsibility for solving product issues impacting our all-in-one privacy solution, whether large or small. In time, you'll formally mentor other engineers, supporting their career growth and the growth of the Backend Team at DuckDuckGo.</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <h1><strong>About You</strong></h1> <ul> <li> <p>7+ years of professional experience, primarily focused on backend systems that power consumer-facing products</p> </li> <li> <p>Product acumen to reason about technical tradeoffs in terms of user impact</p> </li> <li> <p>Familiarity with AI agent tooling: evaluation frameworks, RAG pipelines and prompt engineering</p> </li> <li> <p>A fundamental understanding of complex data structures and algorithms — you can develop and apply new solutions and confidently navigate and improve existing code.</p> </li> <li> <p>Data-driven analytical skills for decision-making, stakeholder alignment, and experiment-oriented delivery</p> </li> <li> <p>Solid project management abilities</p> </li> <li> <p>Excellent written and verbal communication to validate and articulate decisions</p> </li> <li> <p>Previous experience leading and mentoring experienced engineers, supporting their career goals, and unlocking their potential.</p> </li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p> <h1><strong>Compensation</strong></h1> <p>This role is paid on a regional pay scale, in local currency, and stock options:</p> <ul> <li> <p><strong>United States</strong>: $190,500 USD annually</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>United Kingdom</strong>: £134,600 GBP annually</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Canada</strong>: C$253,500 CAD annually</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Europe/Rest of World</strong>: €157,350 EUR annually</p> </li> </ul> <p>In Spain, pay is expected to transition to the EUR scale on January 1, 2027, and in other Europe/Rest of World countries on February 1, 2027.</p> <div>&nbsp;</div> <p>Compensation is transparent across the organization, and all team members within the same professional level and global region receive the same compensation.</p> <div>&nbsp;</div> <p>Eligibility for company-sponsored health benefits is limited to team members based in the United States. This program does not extend to team members located in other countries, such as Canada or the UK.</p> <div>&nbsp;</div> <p>Our<a class="ProsemirrorEditor-link" href="https://duckduckgo.com/assets/hiring/team_support_guide.pdf"> Team Member Support Guide</a> explains how we prioritize your wellbeing including <strong>paid parental leave, office setup, </strong>and <strong>co-working allowances.</strong></p> <div>&nbsp;</div> <p>&nbsp;</p> <h1><strong>Hiring Process</strong></h1> <p>Hiring works best when it's a two-way street. Founded in 2008 and profitable since 2014, our annual revenue is in the hundreds of millions USD and millions use our browser on <a class="ProsemirrorEditor-link" href="https://spreadprivacy.com/introducing-duckduckgo-for-mac/">Mac</a>, <a class="ProsemirrorEditor-link" href="https://spreadprivacy.com/windows-browser-open-beta/">Windows</a>, <a class="ProsemirrorEditor-link" href="https://spreadprivacy.com/duckduckgo-privacy-browser-ios14/">iOS</a>, and <a class="ProsemirrorEditor-link" href="https://spreadprivacy.com/introducing-app-tracking-protection/">Android</a>, our <a class="ProsemirrorEditor-link" href="https://duckduckgo.com/">search engine</a>, and the <a class="ProsemirrorEditor-link" href="https://duckduckgo.com/pro">DuckDuckGo subscription</a>. We also offer private, useful, and optional AI, including <a class="ProsemirrorEditor-link" href="https://duck.ai/">Duck.ai</a>, which lets you chat privately with ChatGPT, Claude, and other AIs, all in one place.</p> <div>&nbsp;</div> <p>Our <a class="ProsemirrorEditor-link" href="https://duckduckgo.com/how-we-work">culture</a> of trust, inclusivity, and empowered project management underpins everything we do, where each team member takes full ownership of their projects, from scoping and execution to postmortem. If you're seeking end-to-end ownership of your work, you've come to the right place!</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <h1><strong>Your Team and Role</strong></h1> <p>Working on the Backend Functional Team, you'll lead complex projects across key company-wide objectives.
